texts.preamble: Manjesh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 9 July, 2020 Author: Ajit Kumar Bench: Ajit Kumar High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 90 Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15923 of 2020 Applicant :- Manjesh Yadav
texts.facts: The applicant is seeking bail in connection with case crime no. 31 of 2020 under Section 272,273,420 IPC, P.S. Ganjdundwara, District Kasganj. The allegation in the first information report against the applicant is of preparation of adulterated milk and the applicant has come to be arrested on the spot as alleged illegal activity was being conducted by him and recovery of material has also made.
texts.arguments: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that after coming into force ofFood Safety and Standards Act, 2006, there is absolute bar of prosecution under any law prior to enforcement of this Act, vide sub clause 97 of cause 2 which is reproduced hereunder: Manjesh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 9 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192904017/ 1 "Section 97 Repeal and Savings (2)- If there is any other law for the time being in force in any State, corresponding to this Act, the same shall upon the commencement of this Act, stand repealed and in such case, the provisions of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 (10 of 1897) shall apply as if such provisions of the State law had been repealed. " It is, therefore, argued by learned counsel for the applicant that in view of aforesaid provision no prosecution can be launched against person indulged in such activity complained of in the present case under the general provisions of Indian penal code. Learned counsel for the applicant has further placed reliance upon a judgement of division bench of Lucknow bench of this Court in Pepsico Food Holdings Pvt. Ltd v. State of U.P, 2010(6) AlJ 13 in which vide paragraph 44, it has been held that after coming into force of Central Act, 2006 the prosecution can be launched only under the said Act .Learned counsel for the applicant submits that law cited above still hold the field and has not been overruled till date. Learned AGA has opposed the bail but could not dispute the aforesaid legal position. In view of overall facts and circumstance of the case, the Court is of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be admitted to bail.

Learned AGA has opposed the bail but could not dispute the aforesaid legal position. In view of overall facts and circumstance of the case, the Court is of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be admitted to bail.
